instruction:
You are tasked to design a state machine that has six states. The state machine should have an input clock signal `clk` and a reset signal `rst_`. The state machine should have an output signal `state_r` which is a 3-bit signal that represents the current state of the state machine. The state machine should follow the state transition diagram below:

```
             +-----+
             |     |
             | IDLE|<----+
             |     |     |
             +--+--+     |
                |        |
                |        |
                |        |
                v        |
             +--+--+     |
             |     |     |
             | SEND|<----+
             |     |     |
             +--+--+     |
                |        |
                |        |
                |        |
                v        |
             +--+--+     |
             |     |     |
             |WAIT1|<----+
             |     |     |
             +--+--+     |
                |        |
                |        |
                |        |
                v        |
             +--+--+     |
             |     |     |
             |UPDAT|<----+
             |  E1 |     |
             |     |     |
             +--+--+     |
                |        |
                |        |
                |        |
                v        |
             +--+--+     |
             |     |     |
             |WAIT2|<----+
             |     |     |
             +--+--+     |
                |        |
                |        |
                |        |
                v        |
             +--+--+     |
             |     |     |
             |UPDAT|<----+
             |  E2 |     |
             |     |     |
             +-----+-----+
```

The state machine should start in the `IDLE` state when reset is asserted. The state machine should transition to the `SEND` state after one clock cycle, then to the `WAIT1` state after another clock cycle, then to the `UPDATE1` state after another clock cycle, then to the `WAIT2` state after another clock cycle, then to the `UPDATE2` state after another clock cycle, and then back to the `IDLE` state after another clock cycle.

Your task is to implement the state machine in Verilog.
